---
name: factory-create-pr
description: Push the current branch and open a GitHub pull request (gh, GITHUB_TOKEN, or a prefilled link; no gh required) or, for a GitLab remote, a merge request (git push options, no glab required), after running the repo's checks. Shows the exact command and asks before pushing.
argument-hint: "[target-branch] [--draft]"
disable-model-invocation: true
allowed-tools: Bash(git status:*), Bash(git branch:*), Bash(git log:*), Bash(git rev-parse:*), Bash(git remote:*), Bash(git fetch:*), Bash(git merge-tree:*), Bash(git symbolic-ref:*)
---

<!-- Generated by sync-kit from factory-kit 0.7.0. Edit plugins/factory-kit in solo-factory, not this copy. -->

Open a pull request (GitHub) or merge request (GitLab) for the current branch. Arguments: `$ARGUMENTS`

1. **Preconditions**: stop and say why if any of these fail.
   - The working tree is clean (`git status --porcelain` prints nothing). If not, suggest
     `/factory-commit`.
   - The current branch isn't the target or any other shared branch (see
     `.claude/skills/factory-checkout-branch/SKILL.md`, step 1). A PR from one shared branch
     into another, such as `staging` → `main`, is a release, not a feature: stop and say so.
   - `origin` exists. Its URL decides the host: GitLab (gitlab.com or a self-hosted GitLab, e.g. a
     host containing `gitlab`) or GitHub (github.com). If you can't tell, ask. Any other host: say
     it's unsupported and stop.
2. **Existing MR/PR**: look for an MR/PR that is already open for this branch.
   - **GitLab**: if `GITLAB_TOKEN` is set (`[ -n "$GITLAB_TOKEN" ]`), run
     `node ".claude/factory-kit/scripts/gitlab-mr.mjs" info`. It prints
     `{ iid, web_url, target_branch, title, draft }` or `null`.
   - **GitHub**: with `gh` logged in, `gh pr view --json number,url,baseRefName`; otherwise, if
     `GITHUB_TOKEN` is set, `node ".claude/factory-kit/scripts/github-pr.mjs" info`, which prints
     `{ number, html_url, base, title, draft }` or `null`.

   If one is open, this run updates it instead of opening a new one, and its target
   (`target_branch` / `base`) is the target. It may be stacked on another feature branch, so don't
   take the target from `CLAUDE.md`. If a target argument names a different branch, say so and ask
   which one is right; a push doesn't change an MR's target. Without a token or CLI, skip this
   step: on GitLab, step 7 route 3 catches an existing MR from the push output.
3. **Target branch**, first match wins:
   - the target of the existing MR from step 2;
   - the first argument that isn't `--draft`;
   - the MR/PR target named in the repo's `CLAUDE.md`;
   - `origin`'s default branch (`git symbolic-ref --short refs/remotes/origin/HEAD`, strip `origin/`).
4. **Up to date**: `git fetch origin`, then `git merge-tree --write-tree origin/<target> HEAD`. If it
   reports conflicts, list the files and stop. Don't rebase on your own.
5. **Checks**: run the check commands `CLAUDE.md` lists for the code this branch touches (for
   example `pnpm test`, `typecheck`, `lint`). If none are listed, run the `test`, `lint` and
   `typecheck` scripts that exist in `package.json`, or say there are none. Stop on any failure.
6. **Title and description**: if the draft `describe-pr` saves (at the path `node ".claude/factory-kit/scripts/report-path.mjs" pr` prints) exists and was written
   for this branch's current commits, use its first line as the title and the rest as the body.
   Otherwise use the subject of the oldest commit on `origin/<target>..HEAD` and no body (and offer
   `/factory-describe-pr` at the end). Trim the title to 100 characters.
7. **Command**:
   - **GitLab, MR already open** (step 2 found one): plain `git push origin HEAD`, with no
     `merge_request.*` options (they only apply when creating an MR). Then, with a draft file,
     `node ".claude/factory-kit/scripts/gitlab-mr.mjs" describe <draft>` to replace its
     description; without one, leave the description as it is. Its title stays as it is; mention
     it if it differs from the draft's.
   - **GitLab, new MR**: git push options can't contain newlines, so a multi-line description needs a
     second channel. Pick the first route that is available, and say which one you picked:
     1. **`glab`** installed and logged in (`glab auth status`): push with MR options (below), then
        `glab mr update <branch> --description "$(tail -n +3 <draft>)"`.
     2. **`GITLAB_TOKEN` set** (check with `[ -n "$GITLAB_TOKEN" ]`; never print it, never ask the
        user to paste a token into the chat): push with MR options, then
        `node ".claude/factory-kit/scripts/gitlab-mr.mjs" describe <draft>`. It finds the open MR
        for this branch through the GitLab API and sets its description. Exit 3 means no token.
     3. **Neither**: plain `git push -u origin HEAD` with no MR options, then
        `node ".claude/factory-kit/scripts/gitlab-mr.mjs" new-url <target> <draft> [--draft] --open`.
        It opens the "New merge request" page in the user's browser with the title and description
        filled in; the user checks it and clicks **Create merge request**. See "Prefilled links"
        below. If the push output says a merge
        request already exists ("View merge request for …"), give its `/edit` link and the body to
        paste instead.

     Push with MR options:
     ```
     git push -u origin HEAD -o merge_request.create -o merge_request.target=<target> -o "merge_request.title=<title>" -o merge_request.remove_source_branch
     ```
     Prefix the title with `Draft: ` for `--draft`. With no draft file, skip the second step; a
     title-only MR is fine.
   - **GitHub**: `git push -u origin HEAD`, then the first route that is available (say which):
     1. **`gh`** installed and logged in (`gh auth status`): `gh pr create --base <target> --title
        "<title>" --body-file <body file>` (add `--draft` for `--draft`; with no body, use
        `--fill-first`). For a PR that is already open, `gh pr edit --body-file <body file>`.
     2. **`GITHUB_TOKEN` set** (never print it, never ask for it in the chat):
        `node ".claude/factory-kit/scripts/github-pr.mjs" create <target> <draft> [--draft]`. It
        opens the PR through the API, or updates the body of the PR already open for this branch.
     3. **Neither**: `node ".claude/factory-kit/scripts/github-pr.mjs" new-url <target> <draft> --open`.
        It opens the "Open a pull request" page in the user's browser with the title and
        description filled in; the user checks it and clicks **Create pull request** (or **Create
        draft pull request** for `--draft`; the link can't set that). Exit 4 means the body made the
        link too long: the link has the title only, so also print the body to paste. See
        "Prefilled links" below.

   **Prefilled links**: the description lives inside the link (`&body=…` /
   `merge_request[description]=…`), so a shortened link loses it.
   - Always pass `--open`. The helper says on stderr whether the browser opened.
   - Whether or not it opened, put the link in your reply **exactly as the helper printed it**,
     however long: one link, never trimmed, re-encoded or rebuilt by hand, and never split into "a
     title link plus the body somewhere else". The user can't see tool output, so never point them
     to "the link printed above".
8. **Show and ask**: show the commit list, the title, the target, and the exact commands. Ask
   "Push and open the MR?" (or "the PR?"; for an existing MR, "Push and update !<iid>?") and run
   them only on a clear yes.
9. **After**: print the MR/PR URL (the existing MR's `web_url`, or from the remote, the helper, or
   the prefilled link). If the description reached GitLab another way than `glab` or `describe`,
   also print the body in a fenced block as a fallback. When route 3 was used, mention that setting
   `GITLAB_TOKEN` or `GITHUB_TOKEN` (exported in the shell profile, see the README for the
   permissions) makes the next MR/PR fully automatic.
   Delete nothing.

Never force-push, never push to the target branch, and never merge.
